proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~5 eV) phosphate that is electronically insulating and chemically compatible with both LiCoO2 and LLZO. Its low reduction and oxidation tendencies should keep the interfacial penalty small at 4.0 V. It is also a well-known protective coating for LCO and is generally stable against Li-rich garnets.

LiF is a wide-gap (~7 eV), electronically insulating fluoride with very low oxidation and reduction tendencies, so it should resist LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. Fluoride coatings are also reported to form thin, stable interphases with garnets. Its simple binary chemistry gives few possible decomposition or contact products, which should keep the contact penalty below the 0.05 eV/atom target. Li3PO4 gave a penalty of 0.099 (bin 4), so this moves to a different anion family.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaauhx) was insulating and wide-gap but failed the penalty criterion at 0.099 eV/non-Li atom, with LLZO decomposing to LaPO4/ZrO2 at the contact. This suggests trying a different anion chemistry, such as a fluoride.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium zirconate. Because it shares Zr4+ with the LLZO garnet, it should avoid the La/Zr-displacement reactions that produced LaPO4, LaF3 and ZrO2 at the LLZO contact for the Li3PO4 and LiF coatings. Its oxide chemistry should also be oxidatively stable against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V, and Li-rich zirconates are reported as protective LCO coatings.
proposal.motivation: Both prior coatings (Li3PO4 penalty 0.099, LiF penalty 0.120) were insulating but gave LLZO contact decomposition to La- and Zr-containing products. This points to choosing a coating whose cation chemistry is closer to the garnet's own Zr sublattice, with an oxide anion.

proposal.hypothesis: LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium aluminate. Al3+ is a known garnet-compatible species, since Al2O3 and Al-bearing phases form thermodynamically tame interphases with LLZO. Unlike the La/Zr-displacing products seen for Li3PO4, LiF and Li2ZrO3, Al is not expected to pull La or Zr out of the garnet. LiAlO2 is also an established oxidatively stable LCO coating at 4.0 V.

The next candidate should be a stable oxide with a different cation, to test whether Al-based chemistry reduces the contact penalty.
